channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Turkey’s Markets Regulator Tightens Rules for Hedge Funds
item.description: Turkey’s markets regulator announced new rules limiting hedge funds’ exposure to related parties and capping concentrated investments, in a bid to address concerns about abnormal returns and repeated warnings from global index providers.
item.dc:creator: Tugce Ozsoy and Baris Balci

item.title: A CEO’s Sudden Exit Spotlights Troubles at German Regional Banks
item.description: In a decade-and-a-half at the helm of Volksbank Brawo, Juergen Brinkmann turned the local German lender into a finance, real estate and investment group spanning hundreds of businesses, including a stake in a gym chain, restaurants and a now-insolvent brewery.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Kahl

item.title: Australian Minister Denies Softer Stance on Data Center Power
item.description: Australia’s Energy Minister Chris Bowen has rejected suggestions the government is softening requirements that future data center developments be powered by renewable energy.
item.dc:creator: Tracy Withers

item.title: Trump Teleprompter Pays $170,000 to End Insider Trading Probe
item.description: A White House teleprompter operator will pay more than $172,000 to end a federal regulator’s probe into alleged well-timed prediction market bets about President Donald Trump’s speeches.
item.dc:creator: Nicola M White

item.title: Indian Bank Stocks Show Widest Exchange Price Gap in Decades
item.description: Shares of some Indian banks closed at sharply different prices on the country’s two largest exchanges on Thursday, the latest sign of dislocation under the new closing auction system.
item.dc:creator: Alex Gabriel Simon

item.title: Wall Street Week | Debt & Consequences, Defying Fiscal Gravity, Hollywood Gets Democratized
item.description: This week, Chrystia Freeland talks with the former finance ministers of the Netherlands and Germany about what it takes to bring spending under control. And, are US deficits now a bigger driver of interest rates than inflation? Plus, as Fed Chair Kevin Warsh makes his debut at the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium, we revisit the story of the wealthiest place in America. Later, the rise of YouTube filmmakers is democratizing discovery, while also flooding the market with more content than audiences can watch. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Former FDIC Chair Sheila Bair on Inflation, Regulatory Landscape
item.description: Former FDIC Chair Sheila Bair discusses inflation and the regulatory landscape in an interview with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: IMF's Georgieva on Warsh's Speech, 'Stubborn' Inflation
item.description: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva says Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh "did a great job" in his Jackson Hole speech. Speaking with Bloomberg's Lisa Abramowicz on "Bloomberg The Close." Georgieva also discusses recent inflation pressures and whether they reflect central bank failure or other forces. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Iran War Hits 6 Month Mark
item.description: Bloomberg Businessweek looks back on the past six months of the US war with Iran, including how President Trump's timeline for the conflict has shifted as talks with Tehran remain mostly stalled. Bloomberg News White House and National Security Editor Michelle Jamrisko discusses how the war has evolved, and what might come next. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Billionaire Gilinski, GeoPark Said to Be Near Venezuela Oil Deal
item.description: Colombia’s richest family is nearing a Venezuela oil deal in conjunction with GeoPark Ltd, a Bogota-based oil company in which it is the largest shareholder with a 28% stake, according to people familiar with the matter who asked for anonymity discussing confidential plans.
item.dc:creator: Mie Dahl

item.title: Tariffs Could Bring Canada Auto "To Its Knees"
item.description: President Trump vowed this week to hike tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks, automotive parts, and steel to 50% at the start of next year as part of an ongoing trade war threat with the country. Linda Hasenfratz, Executive Chair of Linamar, says that after decades of free trade in automotives between he US and Canada, the implementation of such high tariffs would "cripple the industry." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Por qué EE.UU. está detrás de una parte del petróleo de Venezuela
item.description: Aunque Venezuela ya no es la gran potencia petrolera que fue en el pasado, el país cuenta con algunas de las mayores reservas de petróleo del mundo. Desde que Estados Unidos destituyó al entonces presidente venezolano Nicolás Maduro el 3 de enero, ha restablecido las relaciones diplomáticas y está colaborando con el gobierno de la presidenta interina Delcy Rodríguez en Caracas. Pero esa relación está sujeta a numerosas condiciones: el presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, ha calificado a Vene
item.dc:creator: Lucia Kassai and William Norris

item.title: Odd Lots: What’s Behind the Classic Jackson Hole Photo Op?
item.description: For years, the Fed chair would give an address in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, and Wall Street and news organizations wouldn't have a recent photo of the chair to accompany stories. In steps Bloomberg's own Mike McKee. Tracy Alloway, Joe Weisenthal and Tom Keene learn the origin of the now traditional "Fed perp walk." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Science Behind The Markets | Masters in Business with David Booth
item.description: Barry speaks with David Booth, founder and chairman at Dimensional Fund Advisors and author of Stay Calm. They discuss his time at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business where he was the research assistant to American economist and Nobel Laureate Eugene Fama, before leaving to start Dimensional Fund Advisors. They discuss embracing the uncertainty of the markets and the importance of staying the course. David also discusses his philanthropic history and giving back to the places that shaped him. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Threat of a Fed Rate Hike Is Changing the Leadership in Markets, Slimmon Says
item.description: Andrew Slimmon, managing director and head of applied equity advisors at Morgan Stanley, says he's happy with what Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said during his speech at Jackson Hole and he remains consistent. Slimmon says the threat of an interest rate hike is causing a change in leadership in stock markets. He shares more on "Bloomberg The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Funds Add Bullish Gasoline Bets at Fastest Pace in Six Months
item.description: Hedge funds boosted their bullish wagers on US gasoline by the most since the US-Iran war began, Commodity Futures Trading Commission data showed.
item.dc:creator: Will Kubzansky

item.title: Yen Passes 160 Per Dollar to Hit Weakest Level in a Month
item.description: The yen moved past 160 per US dollar to its weakest level in a month, extending a slide that’s erased more than half of its intervention-fueled gains.
item.dc:creator: John Cheng, Ruth Carson and Anya Andrianova

item.title: Panama Canal Congestion Drives Gas Tankers to Unusual Routes
item.description: Growing congestion at the Panama Canal is forcing some gas tankers into unusual journeys, from a rare detour around South America to the possible emergence of shuttling through the waterway.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Lua

item.title: Two-Year Yield Jumps on Warsh’s Inflation Pledge: Markets Wrap
item.description: Wall Street traders sent short-term yields sharply higher as Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh vowed to bring inflation to the target, boosting bets on a rate hike and stabilizing longer-dated bonds.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: India’s Mazumdar-Shaw Is On A Mission to Save Lives
item.description: Known as India’s ‘Queen of Biotech’, Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw built Biocon from a rented garage almost 50 years ago. Today, her multibillion-dollar company is one of the world’s biggest producers of insulin, and a leading force in biosimilars. As she looks at handing over her life’s work to successors, Mazumdar-Shaw talks to Bloomberg’s Haslinda Amin about her pioneering journey as a female entrepreneur in India, her mission to deliver life-saving therapies to patients and what she believes India must do to tackle an AI future. (Source: Bloomberg)
